newsitem.title: PAKISTAN: New communications minister joins Pakistan cabinet.
newsitem.headline: New communications minister joins Pakistan cabinet.

text.p: Pakistani Prime Minister Nawaz Sharif on Thursday brought Azam Hoti into his cabinet as communications minister, adding the first minister from outside his own Pakistan Muslim League (PML) party.

President Farooq Leghari swore in Hoti, who is a member of the Awami National Party (ANP), which is allied to the PML and based in North West Frontier Province, officials said. He was later given the communications portfolio, the state television said.
The ANP, whose patron and effective leader is Abdul Wali Khan, had nominated Hoti for a ministerial slot promised by Sharif as part of the two parties' alliance.
Sharif, apparently unhappy with the choice, had delayed bringing Hoti into his eight-member cabinet, prompting the ANP to hold up formation of a provincial government in North West Frontier Province.
Governments have already taken office in Pakistan's other three provinces of Punjab, Sindh and Balochistan.
Sharif's PML won a landslide victory in a general election on February 3, in which the ANP also did well.
Hoti told APP after the oath-taking ceremony that his party had full confidence in Sharif's leadership and denied there were any differences between their two parties.
